welcome.title: Lashon listens in Hebrew
welcome.lead: Lashon turns your speech into text — in any app, locally on your machine, with nothing uploaded to the cloud.

microphone.title: So Lashon can hear you
microphone.lead: Lashon needs microphone access to transcribe your speech. Let's check it works.

hardware.title: Lashon tunes itself to your machine
hardware.lead: Lashon checks how powerful your machine is and picks models that will run well on it. You can change the choice any time.

tongue.title: The small mark floating on your screen
tongue.lead: This is the tongue. It breathes quietly at rest, blooms into sound waves as it listens, and settles to dots while transcribing. Drag it to any corner.

hotkey.title: One key opens dictation
hotkey.lead: A single press of Ctrl+Space opens listening. Speak Hebrew — and when you finish, the text appears wherever the cursor is.

practice.title: Try it now
practice.lead: Press Ctrl+Space and say a short sentence in Hebrew — I'll show you here exactly what Lashon heard.

done.title: That's it — you know how to use Lashon
done.lead: You can always reopen this tutorial from the tray menu, next to the clock.

warmup.label: Lashon is getting ready for first use
warmup.hint: A one-time download — the next launch is instant.

mic.ready: Excellent — Lashon can hear your microphone.
mic.noDevice: No microphone found. Connect one and check again.
mic.blocked: Lashon couldn't open the microphone. Grant microphone access in your system settings, then check again.
mic.hint: Recording stays on your machine — no audio is sent anywhere.

hardware.override: Lashon picked the marked tier. You can choose a different one:

states.idle: At rest — the mark breathes gently
states.listening: Listening — the mark blooms into sound waves
states.transcribing: Transcribing — the mark settles to dots
states.hint: The colour stays constant — only the shape changes with what Lashon is doing.
states.dictateBlurb: What you say is typed wherever the cursor is.
states.commandBlurb: A single sentence that gets done — "open Slack", "mute everything".
states.chatBlurb: Free-form voice conversation. Memory stays with you.

howto.step1: Press once — the tongue starts listening.
howto.step2: Speak Hebrew in a normal voice.
howto.step3: Stop speaking, or press again — and the text is dictated.
howto.fineprint: These are the three chords. We'll only practise the first one for now.

practice.or: Or anything else you like — Lashon listens to it all.
practice.hint: You don't have to practise to continue — but it's much more fun to see it work.
practice.heardHint: This is what Lashon heard. In real use it would be typed wherever your cursor is.

live.preparing: Lashon is still getting ready. One moment…
live.error: Something went wrong. Try again — press Ctrl+Space.
live.done: Excellent — your text was dictated. You can continue.
live.waiting: Waiting. Press Ctrl+Space and say a sentence.

tips.drag: Drag the tongue to a screen corner — it snaps to the edge.
tips.reopen: This tutorial is always available from the tray menu.

general.title: General
general.languageHint: Choose the language Lashon's interface is shown in. The change applies to every window immediately.

hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.intro: The hardware tier sets how Lashon runs speech recognition — probing the GPU, or staying on the CPU. Lashon never changes it silently; the choice is yours.
hardware.sttDeviceGpu: On this tier, speech recognition uses the GPU when one is available.
hardware.sttDeviceCpu: On this tier, speech recognition runs on the CPU.
hardware.restartToApply: Restart Lashon for this change to take effect.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
shortcuts.dictationHint: The key combination that opens and closes listening from any app.
shortcuts.commandHint: Press, speak a command — the LLM picks tools to run it on your PC.

invalid.no-modifier: A shortcut must include a modifier key — Ctrl, Alt or Shift.
invalid.no-key: A shortcut must include one key besides the modifiers.
invalid.malformed: That combination isn't valid. Try another.
invalid.reserved: That combination is reserved by the operating system. Choose another.

wakeword.title: Wake words
wakeword.intro: Lashon listens for two independent wake words — one starts hands-free dictation, the other runs a Command-mode tool chain. Pick a different classifier for each slot.
wakeword.enableHint: When on, Lashon listens in the background for this wake word.
wakeword.modelHint: Pick which classifier this slot listens for. The other slot's model is hidden so each word maps to one mode.
wakeword.moreOptionsHint: These openWakeWord classifiers are released under a non-commercial licence (CC-BY-NC-4.0). Installing one limits your use of it to non-commercial purposes.
wakeword.ncTooltip: Licensed under CC-BY-NC-4.0 — non-commercial use only.
wakeword.installConfirm:
Install {name}?

This model is licensed {license}. By installing it, you agree to use it for non-commercial purposes only.
wakeword.libraryHint: Looking for other wake words? Browse
wakeword.sensitivityHint: Higher sensitivity detects the wake word more readily, but may respond to false activations.

dictation.title: Dictation slot
dictation.hint: When this wake word fires, the next thing you say is typed into the focused field — like the dictation hotkey.

command.title: Command slot
command.hint: When this wake word fires, the next thing you say runs as a Command-mode tool chain (open apps, click buttons, send messages…).

llm.title: Language models
llm.intro: Lashon can call a language model for two different modes — Command mode (M8) and Chat mode (M8). The cloud is always opt-in and badged, and your API keys never touch settings.json.
llm.commandHint: The model that turns voice commands into PC actions.
llm.chatHint: The model that answers free-form questions in conversation.
llm.cloudBadgeTooltip: Cloud provider — your text is sent to a remote server.
llm.hebrewOkTooltip: Provider verified to handle Hebrew well.
llm.hebrewBasicTooltip: Provider accepts Hebrew but quality is unverified.
llm.apiKeySaved: Key saved to your OS keychain
llm.recommendedHint: Fastest and most accurate model for Command mode — Lashon picks {model} by default.
llm.modelsShowingOf: Showing {shown} of {total} models from provider (filtered to chat models, newest first)
llm.baseUrlHint: Leave blank to use the vendor's default endpoint.
llm.ollamaNotRunning: Ollama isn't running on this machine. Install and start it first.
llm.noProvider: Pick a provider to test the connection.
llm.noKeyForCloud: Cloud providers need an API key. Enter one to activate.

localLlm.runtimeMissing: This build was compiled without the local LLM runtime. Use a different provider or rebuild with `--features local-llm`.
localLlm.downloadRequired: Model not on disk. Download once — it stays for next time.

recipes.title: Recipes
recipes.intro: Stored desktop workflows. Say the trigger and Lashon runs the recipe deterministically — no LLM in the loop.
recipes.noMatch: No recipes match the current filters.
recipes.deleteBody: The recipe {name} will be removed from disk. This can't be undone.

steps.slotLegend: Pills are filled in when you press Run.
steps.commentPlaceholder: Add a comment for this step…
steps.notYetRunnableTitle: Not supported by the v1 runtime — coming in v1.1
steps.errorParseBody: The YAML is invalid. Open the file to fix it.
steps.errorEmptyBody: The recipe parsed but has no steps. Edit the file to add some.

bodyExtras.screenshotNote: (the image lands on the clipboard — no variables)

about.title: About
about.tagline: A local-first voice assistant that listens in Hebrew.
about.localFirst: All processing happens on your machine. No recording or text is sent to the cloud.

voice.title: Voice corrections
voice.intro: Token-level substitutions applied to the STT transcript before either the recipe cascade or the LLM planner sees it. Useful for proper nouns Whisper keeps mishearing ("cloud" instead of "claude"), contact-name homonyms, and any word that consistently lands wrong.

transcript.cancelHint: Esc · cancel before the command runs

tierA.name: Studio
tierA.desc: A powerful NVIDIA GPU. Everything runs locally, at full speed.

tierB.name: Workstation
tierB.desc: A mid-range NVIDIA GPU. Local processing with compact models.

tierC.name: Office
tierC.desc: No NVIDIA GPU. Local dictation; cloud is recommended for advanced commands.

tierD.name: Minimal
tierD.desc: Basic hardware. Local dictation; other capabilities via the cloud.
